title: ALMA Host Galaxy Observation of the Off-axis Gamma-Ray Burst XRF 020903
question: Whether the submillimeter/millimeter radio properties (dust continuum, CO emission, molecular gas mass, and gas depletion timescale) of the off-axis GRB XRF 020903 host galaxy resemble those of classical GRB host galaxies, supporting an identical origin.

data.sensitivity: 3-sigma upper limits: 0.032 mJy at 113 GHz, 0.061 mJy at 224 GHz, 0.57 mJy for 180 km/s CO velocity-integrated map

what.value: Redshift z=0.251 and HST optical measurements of XRF 020903 host galaxy

evidence.quote: The redshift of $z=0.251$ (cite: soderberg2004) was measured via optical spectroscopic observation observations.

evidence.loc: IR Luminosity and Star Formation Rate (SFR) with GRB Host Galaxies
evidence.quote: In terms of the SED for describing optical measurements, we primarily used the HST measurement (cite: soderberg2004), because the ground-based multicolor measurements were affected by the nearby galaxies, as reported by (cite: bersier06).

what.value: Spatially resolved metallicities of four regions in XRF 020903 host galaxy (8.1 +/- 0.1 for burst site and ~8.2 for remaining regions)

evidence.quote: Using line diagnostics (cite: thorp2018), the low metallicities for all of four regions were measured to be $8.1\pm0.1$ for the burst site and $\sim$8.2 for the remaining regions.

what.value: H-alpha, [O II], or UV SFR measurements for XRF 020903 (2.65 M_sun yr^-1) and reference GRB host galaxies

evidence.quote: This estimation is consistent with the measurement (2.65$M_{\ensuremath{\odot}}$ yr$^{-1}$) using $H_{\alpha}$ or rather small (cite: ghost).

recipe.goal: Calibrate and image ALMA continuum and CO(1-0) observations
recipe.method: Run ALMA Science Pipeline calibration, merge execution blocks where needed (GRB 050709), and image continuum and a 180 km s^-1 CO(1-0) velocity-integrated map using TCLEAN with Briggs weighting
key_parameters: CO(1-0) velocity integration width = 180 km s^-1

recipe.goal: Measure continuum fluxes, upper limits, and extract CO spectrum
recipe.method: Measure total flux for detections using CASA imfit, estimate RMS noise for nondetections using CASA imstat, and extract CO(1-0) spectrum within a 0".8 radius aperture centered on the host galaxy
key_parameters: Spectral extraction aperture centered at R.A. = 22h48m42s.37, decl. = -20d46'08".72 with radius 0".8

recipe.goal: Derive IR luminosity and star formation rate from dust continuum
recipe.method: Apply target redshift to luminosity-dependent IR SED templates from Chary & Elbaz (2001) to constrain L_IR from continuum flux/limits, then convert L_IR to SFR using Kennicutt (1998)
assumptions: Cosmological parameters H0 = 70 km s^-1, Omega_0 = 0.3, Omega_lambda = 0.7
Chary & Elbaz (2001) luminosity-dependent IR SED templates without scaling
Kennicutt (1998) conversion SFR(M_sun yr^-1) = 1.7 x 10^-10 L_IR / L_sun

recipe.goal: Derive CO luminosity, molecular gas mass, gas fraction, and gas depletion timescale
recipe.method: Calculate L'_CO upper limit using Solomon & Vanden Bout (2005) equation, convert to M_gas using metallicity-dependent and Galactic alpha_CO factors, and compute gas depletion timescale t_depl = M_gas / SFR
assumptions: Metallicity-dependent alpha_CO from harmonic mean of Genzel et al. (2012) and Bolatto et al. (2013): alpha_CO = 15 M_sun (K km s^-1 pc^2)^-1 for region A (12+log(O/H) = 8.1) and alpha_CO = 9.6 for regions B, C, D (12+log(O/H) ~ 8.2); Galactic alpha_CO = 4.4
H-alpha SFR = 2.65 M_sun yr^-1 used for M_gas-SFR and depletion timescale comparison

score_reason: Standard ALMA pipeline calibration and TCLEAN imaging with stated robust parameter (0.5), beam sizes, velocity integration width (180 km/s), and explicit analytic equations for L'_CO, M_gas, and SFR, though some archival project codes and minor TCLEAN parameters are omitted.
rediscovery_reason: Public ALMA data with explicit project codes for XRF 020903 (2015.1.01254.S) and GRB 050709 (2016.1.01333.S), standard pipeline calibration, standard Briggs r=0.5 imaging, and straightforward upper limit and analytical luminosity/mass derivations.
